sources.title: R. C. Majumdar, Jodhpur inscription of Pratihara Bauka, Epigraphia Indica XVIII
sources.note: Primary edition, printed pages 87 to 99. Pages 87, 88, 96 to 99 directly read; p97 scan visually inspected, saved ei18-p97.jpg. Dated Vikrama 894, conventionally 837 CE; public date about 837. Sanskrit line 22 Utkirnna/utkīrṇṇā and p99 translation; avoids restoration brackets elsewhere in that line. Whole EI XVIII grouped, along with Debiprasad earlier edition.

sources.title: Munshi Debiprasad, Jodhpur Inscription of the Pratihara Bauka, JRAS (1894)
sources.note: Original 1894 paper extract directly read: inscription reused upside down in Jodhpur city wall, discovery about two years earlier. Grouped with later EI XVIII edition of the same inscription.

sources.title: D. R. Bhandarkar, Ghatiyala inscriptions of Kakkuka, Epigraphia Indica IX
sources.note: Printed pages 277 to 281, especially 278 to 279 directly read. 861 market, settlement promises and four Ganapati images. Colonial stereotypes about Ahirs explicitly rejected; uncertain prakriti=Kshatriya gloss omitted. Same work as Buchkala below.

sources.title: D. R. Bhandarkar, Buchkala inscription of Nagabhatta, Epigraphia Indica IX, pp.198 to 200
sources.note: Printed page 199 directly read. VS872/815, queen Jayavali, temple construction and unspecified thing installed; not automatically an idol. Names Bhumbhuvaka/Haragupta/Avanganaka not needed. No confident inference about local capital or exact personal overlord beyond dated reign.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Western Circle Progress Report for year ending 31 March 1907
sources.note: Original scanned government report, title and printed page 34 read through indexed original. Mandor-area Pratiharas distinguished from Kanauj dynasty; Ghatiyala Jain temple, Prakrit inscription and stone pillar construction. Full PDF opens image-only.

sources.title: Government of India, Incredible India: Dausa
sources.note: Official description accessed directly through indexed text; Chand Baori eighth/ninth century. Exact step totals and depth not used because competing official measurements exist.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Harsat Mata ka Mandir
sources.note: Full original institutional description accessed in indexed search. ASI dates temple eighth century; public explicitly places this example before the atlas interval. Music/dance/garden scenes as art, not household diary. Grouped with ASI monument descriptions below for conservative budget.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Mandor Fort
sources.note: Original institutional text read through search index: excavated temple three terraces, seventh/eighth-century sanctum, ninth/tenth and twelfth-century restoration. Do not conflate much earlier Krishna pillars or modern standing complex with ninth-century building.

sources.title: Anil K. Pokharia and colleagues, Variable monsoons and human adaptations (2020)
sources.note: Direct full13-page paper read: printed manuscript pages4 to 6, Table1 and Fig2. PhaseII800 to 1300 is much broader than atlas800 to 900. Existing Rajput kingdoms packet already uses same work; preserve cumulative allowance. DOI10.1177/0959683620919976.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Separate regional-context card for800 to 900 only. No alias with rajput-kingdoms1000 to 1279, named dynasty cards or later Rajputana/Rajputs.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Sole imported world800 polygon bbox91.6515,12.3270,107.4881,24.8881. Includes ChiangMai/Vientiane, excludes all Indian reference sites. Public overview plainly marks displaced outline; no Southeast Asian community identified as Rajput.
batchIdentityNotes.dating: Contemporary anchors815,about837,861. Mandor core predates slice with dated later repairs; Chandravati material broad800 to 1300. No homogeneous Rajput identity retrojected, no fall in900.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: No household medical practice, universal schools or historical toilets securely established. Modern visitor toilets in ASI facilities sections are explicitly excluded.
